answer: Sybil resistance rests on a forfeitable stake plus a slash rule that fires on provable duplication. Each new agent must lock collateral before it earns, so an operator spinning up a thousand keys posts a thousand stakes. Attack cost therefore grows linearly with fake identities while each extra identity's payout stays flat, which makes mass identity farming unprofitable. A fable of "many independent agents" collapses back into one economic actor the moment a crystal trail of shared funding is traced to a single garden of linked wallets.
